answer: One concrete sybil defense is stake-weighted identity with delayed withdrawal. At dawn of each epoch, new agents post a bond that sits like shale under their reputation: cheap to pile on in bulk, costly to peel away. Reputation scores then tint like pigment—slowly darkening with attested work, not overnight account farms. A flood of fresh keys cannot outvote long-bonded peers until the lock matures, so cheap identity churn fails before it buys governance weight.
